characters.description: Frisha’s formidable suitor and the organizer of the tournament journey. He adopts the manner of an exceptionally powerful noble and uses the deference he attracts to improve Frisha’s treatment among her highborn relatives.
characters.name: Rezkin

characters.description: Rezkin’s intended partner and General Marcum’s heir through his sister. Rezkin presents her as his girlfriend before her noble relatives, while she defends the practical abilities they dismiss and recognizes that he is performing a role without knowing its full purpose.
characters.name: Frisha

characters.description: Frisha's sworn escort and Rezkin's friend. His honor is challenged by one of Frisha's noble cousins, but Rezkin publicly affirms both his oath and their friendship while placing him within the expedition's protected inner circle.
characters.name: Tamarin Blackwater

characters.description: A warrior traveling with Rezkin's party who continues training for combat. She recognizes that his high-noble manner is a performance without knowing its full purpose.
characters.name: Reaylin de Voss

characters.description: The wary heir of the Duke of Wellenven, traveling with the party to the tournament.
characters.name: Tieran Nirius

characters.description: An army officer accompanying the travelers on their journey to the tournament.
characters.name: Captain Jimson

characters.description: Frisha’s older cousin and the future head of her noble house. Though initially class-conscious, he responds strongly to Rezkin’s approval and begins treating him as a model of honorable highborn behavior.
characters.name: Frisha's house heir

characters.description: A young noble traveling with his siblings to compete at the tournament. He is interested in the competition and follows his older brother’s lead.
characters.name: Frisha's younger cousin

characters.description: A status-conscious noblewoman who disparages commoners and pursues Rezkin despite his declared relationship with Frisha. Her insults toward Frisha and Tamarin provoke a public rebuke from Rezkin.
characters.name: Frisha's female cousin

characters.description: A young noble who travels to the tournament with Frisha's cousins as their friend.
characters.name: Young noble friend

characters.description: The reigning king of Ashai. At the opening of the book, his growing taxes and military musters are contributing to instability, while serious accusations concerning King Bordran and Prince Thresson remain allegations rather than established events.
characters.name: King Caydean

characters.description: The only fortress striker known to have escaped Rezkin's final test. He remains missing and is Rezkin's principal lead to the purpose of the hidden fortress, the orders given there, and the fate intended for its trainees.
characters.name: Striker Farson

characters.description: A stranded journeyman mage who wanted to follow life magic but possesses a powerful destructive affinity. He is reluctant to kill and cannot heal effectively himself, yet his instruction lets Reaylin direct her dangerous new gift, prompting Rezkin to hire him.
characters.name: Wesson

characters.description: A badly beaten prisoner rushed through a mob trial after admitting that he killed the mayor's son. The legal question of murder remains untested when Rezkin challenges the proceeding, removes the magistrate, and takes Kai into custody for an investigation.
characters.name: Kai

characters.description: An Ashai officer traveling with Rezkin's party. When Kai denounces King Caydean and questions the royal succession, Drascon objects, demonstrating his continued formal loyalty to the reigning monarch.
characters.name: Lieutenant Drascon

characters.description: The widow of Lord Gadderand and a former Razor Edges guildmaster. She approaches Rezkin under the mistaken belief that the Raven has ordered her to observe him.
characters.name: Hilith Gadderand

characters.description: The noble who hosts Tieran at his Scutton estate during the tournament.
characters.name: Duke of Scutton

characters.description: A master swordsmith in Scutton who grants Rezkin access to exceptional weapons after seeing evidence of his skill.
characters.name: Scutton swordsmith

characters.description: A guest at the Duke of Scutton's estate and the youngest son of another duke. He covertly directs mage power at Rezkin when Rezkin answers Tieran's summons.
characters.name: Duke of Scutton's guest

characters.description: A common-born fifth-tier competitor trained by her late father, once a royal guard in their homeland. She places seventh in her division and earns recognition as a swordmaster, drawing the younger count's admiration and Kai's interest as a recruit.
characters.name: Young swordwoman

characters.description: A surviving trainer from Rezkin's hidden fortress who recognizes his former pupil. He believes Rezkin was created to serve an unknown master and may hold crucial knowledge about the purpose of the training and the instructions that never reached Rezkin.
characters.name: Former fortress striker

characters.description: The leader of an Eastern Mountains contingent. Dark Tidings bests him using his own axe, then brings him back from death. By keeping the axe, Dark Tidings holds the symbol of temporary chieftaincy.
characters.name: Eastern Mountains chieftain

characters.description: Two of seven royal strikers sent to arrest Dark Tidings for treason. Unlike their companions, they refuse to begin fighting before examining his evidence of authority, separating themselves from the immediate attack.
characters.name: Two aligned strikers

characters.description: A member of the traveling military escort who faces a choice when Dark Tidings organizes the flight from Scutton. After being told that no one is compelled to follow, Millens chooses to remain with the escape column.
characters.name: Millens

characters.description: A merchant-ship captain who once commanded in the royal navy. He lost that post after King Bordran died because he spoke against the succeeding government, and now agrees to carry Rezkin's refugees toward safety.
characters.name: Merchant-ship captain

characters.description: The man behind the Raven plans a masked tournament identity named Dark Tidings to attract striker attention while avoiding recognition.
characters.name: Rezkin

characters.description: An Ashai general whose approval Rezkin sought before marrying Frisha. He rejected the proposal despite respecting Rezkin professionally.
characters.name: General Marcum

recaps.ending: Rezkin wins both the melee and fifth-tier tournament as Dark Tidings. When seven strikers attempt to arrest him, two wait to examine King Bordran's certificate and ultimately swear fealty, while the other five die fighting him. Caydean's forces turn the arena lockdown into a wider campaign against foreigners, so Rezkin organizes fighters, companions, and spectators into an escape column. They breach the Duke of Scutton's estate, evacuate surviving captives from its slave prison, and flee through the sea cave. The young swordwoman executes the duke for his crimes and her father's apparent murder. Frisha’s younger cousin is killed while shielding the young swordwoman during the final fight. A former royal-navy commander carries the survivors away on his merchant ship. At sea, Rezkin unmasks before the traveling party and identifies himself as Dark Tidings and the true king. Frisha, Tam, Reaylin, Wesson, Kai, Tieran, Jimson, Drascon, Millens, the aligned strikers, and the other refugees are fugitives pursued by the royal navy. Caydean has targeted their houses and General Marcum has fled. Rezkin's exact royal lineage, Bordran's complete plan, Striker Farson's location, and the fortress order remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Rezkin leads Frisha and their companions toward the king's tournament while cultivating noble allies and investigating the authority left to him by King Bordran. Kai, a former striker, identifies Rezkin as the rightful king, and Wesson verifies both his royal certificate and his unusual magic. In Scutton, Rezkin competes secretly as Dark Tidings, builds public support, survives surveillance and poison plots, and discovers the host duke's hidden slave prison. King Caydean's attempt to arrest Dark Tidings expands into mass detention of foreigners. Rezkin wins the tournament, kills five attacking strikers, and leads an armed evacuation through the duke's estate. The duke is executed, surviving captives are rescued, and Frisha's younger cousin dies protecting the young swordwoman. The refugees escape by sea, where Rezkin reveals that he is both Dark Tidings and the true king. Caydean moves against their families and sends the royal navy after them as they seek foreign refuge.

recaps.text: Previously: Rezkin emerged from a hidden upbringing with extraordinary martial and practical training, two royal blades, and authority connected to the late King Bordran. He formed close ties with Frisha, her sworn escort Tamarin Blackwater, the warrior Reaylin de Voss, and Captain Jimson. Rezkin sought General Marcum's approval to marry Frisha, but Marcum rejected the proposal despite respecting Rezkin professionally. Rezkin also operated a covert network as the Raven, while keeping his identities and purposes divided among those around him. King Caydean ruled Ashai after Bordran's death, Prince Thresson was missing, and serious questions remained about the royal succession. Rezkin's former trainer Striker Farson was still at large and represented the best available lead to the hidden fortress, its final orders, and the reason Rezkin had been prepared there. As the new journey begins, Rezkin is committed to protecting his friends, understanding the authority he carries, and taking the group to the king's tournament.

Rezkin takes command of the tournament voyage by assuming the manner of a powerful high noble. He uses the travelers' deference to defend Frisha and Tamarin from class-based insults and to encourage Frisha's relatives and Tieran Nirius to treat them with respect. When a falling beam injures Rezkin, Reaylin's natural healing power awakens. She resists the discovery, but later heals a donkey and a gravely injured prisoner under the instruction of Wesson, a reluctant destructive mage whom Rezkin hires as her teacher. The prisoner, Kai, has admitted killing the mayor's son, but Rezkin stops a corrupt and hurried trial so the charge can be investigated. Kai recognizes signs that Rezkin possesses royal sword-bearer authority and demands proof. Under a mage oath, Wesson authenticates King Bordran's certificate and two Shailen blades, confirms that they are keyed to Rezkin, and finds that Bordran freed them from the reigning king's bond. Kai swears fealty to Rezkin as king. Rezkin accepts responsibility for protecting him but rejects the title and orders secrecy. Kai then accuses Caydean of killing Bordran and abusing Prince Thresson, though neither claim has been independently established.

Rezkin uncovers evidence that the mayor and dismissed magistrate covered up the rape committed by the mayor's son. He kills the two officials while making their deaths appear to result from a mutual struggle. The baron later dismisses the charge against Kai, who joins the voyage. During shipboard practice, Rezkin defeats Kai and exposes his mastery of two blades. Kai identifies Rezkin's dead fortress trainers as strikers and learns that Rezkin killed fourteen of them during his final test while Farson escaped. Rezkin does not know who issued the final order or whom it truly targeted. Tamarin recoils from Rezkin's history, but Frisha argues that killings carried out as lawful duties require context. After reflection, Tam apologizes and swears fealty to Rezkin. Economic decline, taxation, and military musters under Caydean are worsening across Ashai. Kai tells the young nobles that Bordran named an alternative successor, while concealing that it is Rezkin. Wesson notices a possible magical effect that discourages scrutiny of Rezkin's assumed roles. At Port Manai, Hilith Gadderand approaches Rezkin believing the Raven ordered her to spy on him. Wesson again authenticates the claimant's authority, and Reaylin reveals her rebel allegiance before swearing to the unnamed true king through Rezkin.

Rezkin accepts Reaylin's oath on behalf of the unnamed true king but refuses similar offers from Frisha and the young nobles because association with the claimant could endanger their houses. Wesson identifies the subtle spell on Rezkin: a plausible disguise or assumed role becomes unusually convincing, and observers are discouraged from questioning it. As the Raven, Rezkin takes command of the Razor Edges and then establishes control in Scutton by destroying the defiant Ghouls guild and threatening the Stalkers. Meanwhile, Reaylin begins functioning as the party's healer, Wesson explores constructive applications for his destructive power, and Tieran becomes increasingly receptive to a lawful alternative to Caydean. The party reaches Scutton for the king's tournament, where Tieran stays with the Duke of Scutton. Rezkin plans to enter without letting the strikers recognize him. He and his closest allies choose the name Dark Tidings, and a swordsmith supplies a distinctive black blade. Wesson creates a mask and enchantments that hide the wearer's features and prevent observers from remembering the disguised voice. With black clothing, altered hair, the new sword, and the secured mask, Dark Tidings is ready for the tournament while most of Rezkin's companions believe he will not compete.

Dark Tidings registers for the melee and fifth-tier duels, passes the trial by disarming a royal-guard captain, and sponsors qualified commoners who cannot afford entry. His skill attracts public support and close attention from Caydean's strikers, though he repeatedly evades their surveillance. At the Duke of Scutton's estate, another noble guest directs mage power at Rezkin. Rezkin then finds triania poison on Tieran's intended practice equipment and moves him to safety. After seeing Bordran's certificate and learning about Rezkin's concealment spell, Tieran realizes that Rezkin is the named heir. Wesson's blood test establishes that the two men are close relatives without determining the exact relationship. Tieran swears fealty, and Rezkin tells him that he is Dark Tidings. Poison later strikes Frisha's house heir before a tournament bout, but Rezkin administers an antidote and the count recovers. Rumors of a true king spread while Rezkin covertly pressures the host duke to support the rising claimant. Investigating heavily warded passages beneath the duke's manor, Rezkin, Wesson, and Tieran discover a hidden slave prison. Dozens have been confined and starved, only a fraction appear likely to survive, and records expose the duke's trade and a concealed sea route.

Rezkin covertly supplies the surviving captives while arranging a ship and preparing to leave after the tournament. A common-born fifth-tier swordwoman learns that Rezkin is both the true king and Dark Tidings, swears fealty, and accepts his guardianship. A former fortress striker then recognizes Rezkin and claims he was created to serve an unknown master. Rezkin shows him Bordran's certificate and offers the strikers a lawful basis for changing allegiance, but the incomplete fortress plan remains unexplained. Dark Tidings wins the tournament. Seven strikers try to arrest him for treason; two pause to inspect his proof and swear fealty, while he kills the other five. Caydean's forces seal the arena and begin detaining foreigners for ransom, enslavement, or death. Rezkin forms an armed escape column, fights through Scutton, and breaches the Duke of Scutton's estate. The young swordwoman executes the duke, and the group evacuates surviving captives through the sea cave. Frisha's younger cousin dies protecting the swordwoman during the final fight. The refugees board a merchant ship commanded by a former royal-navy officer. At sea, Rezkin removes the Dark Tidings mask and confirms to the travelers that he is the true king. Caydean has targeted their families and replaced General Marcum, who fled rather than obey. With the royal navy pursuing, Rezkin's coalition sails toward foreign refuge.

characters.description: A mediator in her mid-twenties, back at the Junipero Serra Mission Academy in Carmel, this time on the staff as its guidance counselor. She still sees and speaks with the dead, though she has not had to do much about it lately, and she is engaged to Jesse and planning a wedding. Years of handling hauntings alone have left her with the habit of dealing with a problem first and mentioning it to nobody, which is the habit the book tests.
characters.name: Susannah Simon

characters.description: Alive. The nineteenth-century ghost Suze grew up with is a living man in the present day, working in medicine and training as a doctor, and engaged to Suze. He has built a modern life without losing the manners, principles and protectiveness of the century he was born in, and he is not willing to be kept out of anything that concerns her.
characters.name: Jesse de Silva

characters.description: A shifter Suze has known since she was sixteen, now grown, wealthy and back in Carmel with business interests in the town and an interest in Suze that never went away. He knows more about what people like them can do than anyone else alive, and he has always been willing to use what he knows as leverage.
characters.name: Paul Slater

characters.description: Still the principal of the Mission Academy and still a mediator, considerably older now, and the person who gave Suze her job. He has known what she is longer than anyone.
characters.name: Father Dominic

characters.description: Suze's oldest friend from her school days in Carmel, now working as a journalist, with the same instinct for what is really going on and the same willingness to dig for it.
characters.name: CeeCee Webb

characters.description: CeeCee's oldest friend and Suze's, still part of their lives well past the end of school.
characters.name: Adam McTavish

characters.description: Suze's stepfather, the contractor who married her mother and restored the old house she grew up in, still cheerful and still cooking for whoever turns up.
characters.name: Andy Ackerman

characters.description: Widowed young, remarried to Andy, and delighted that her daughter is finally getting married. She has never been told what Suze can do.
characters.name: Suze's mother

characters.description: The eldest of Suze's three stepbrothers, grown up and settled into work. Suze has called him Sleepy since she was sixteen.
characters.name: Jake Ackerman

characters.description: The stepbrother closest to Suze in age, an adult now and no easier to get along with. Suze has called him Dopey since she was sixteen.
characters.name: Brad Ackerman

characters.description: The youngest stepbrother, the twelve-year-old encyclopedia now grown into an academic career, and still the one Suze actually likes. She has called him Doc since she was sixteen.
characters.name: David Ackerman

recaps.ending: The haunting at the school is resolved, and Suze and Jesse are married. Paul does not get what he demanded of her, and the leverage he built the whole approach on stops working once Suze stops handling it alone and lets Jesse and Father Dominic in. What Paul is left holding is his knowledge of what shifters can do, which he still has and still intends to use, so he remains a permanent presence at the edge of their lives rather than a problem that has been closed. Suze finishes the book with the marriage she has been waiting years for, a job at the school where she grew up, and the understanding that being an adult with a career has not stopped the dead coming to her, only changed what it costs her when they do.
recaps.in_short: Suze Simon is in her mid-twenties, working as the guidance counselor at her old school in Carmel and engaged to Jesse, who is alive in the present day and training as a doctor. Two things arrive at once: a student at the school is plainly being tormented by something nobody else can see, and Paul Slater comes back to town. Paul has acquired the old house Suze grew up in, the one where Jesse died, and is entirely willing to destroy it; he offers Suze terms for keeping it, which she does not want and does not tell Jesse about. Handling both alone, as she has always done, makes both worse. The haunting at the school turns dangerous and Suze is drawn fully back into the work she thought she had left behind as a teenager. In the end the case is resolved, Paul does not get what he wanted, and Suze and Jesse are married.

recaps.text: Susannah Simon is a mediator: she sees and speaks with the dead, and ghosts with unfinished business seek her out. As a teenager she moved from Brooklyn to Carmel-by-the-Sea when her widowed mother married Andy Ackerman, gaining three stepbrothers and a bedroom already occupied by the ghost of a young man murdered there in 1850. At the Junipero Serra Mission Academy she found that the principal, Father Dominic, was a mediator too, and the two worked through years of hauntings together while disagreeing about method: he counseled the dead, she fought them. She eventually learned the ghost's story. He was Hector de Silva, called Jesse, killed on the orders of the cousin he was engaged to and buried in the backyard; when his remains were found and laid to rest he was free to move on and stayed instead, for her. She also met Paul Slater, who has the same ability, calls it shifting, and knows far more about it than Father Dominic. Paul used that knowledge against her, threatening to travel into the past and prevent Jesse's murder so that Suze would never meet him. Suze went after him, and what came out of it was Jesse alive in the present day, with a life to build and a future with Suze in it. Years later they are engaged, and Paul is still out there.

Suze is in her mid-twenties and back at the Mission Academy, this time as its guidance counselor, working for a much older Father Dominic. Jesse is alive, training as a doctor, and the two are engaged and planning their wedding. Neither of them has needed her old abilities much in recent years. That changes on two fronts at once: a student she is counseling is plainly being tormented by something nobody else can see, and Paul Slater comes back to Carmel.

Paul has acquired the old house Suze grew up in, the one where Jesse died and where his body lay for a century and a half, and he is entirely willing to have it torn down. He offers Suze terms for saving it, terms she has no intention of accepting and no intention of repeating to Jesse. Keeping it to herself is the same instinct that got her through her teens, and it works no better now. At the school, the haunting of her student proves older and more tangled than a straightforward angry ghost, and Suze finds herself doing the work she thought she had grown out of, now with a professional role and somebody else's child to answer for.

The case at the school turns dangerous and stops being containable, and Suze's habit of managing everything alone costs her as much as it ever did. Jesse, who is neither a ghost nor a teenager any more, is not willing to be protected out of the situation, and what Suze has not told him about Paul comes out. Father Dominic, older and less able to help than he once was, is drawn in as well. Paul's approach hardens as it becomes clear that the price he named is not going to be paid, and the wedding Suze is supposed to be arranging keeps colliding with everything else.

The haunting at the school is resolved and Suze and Jesse are married. Paul does not get what he demanded; once Suze stops handling him alone and brings Jesse and Father Dominic in, the leverage he had built the whole approach on stops working. He is not finished with them, though: what he knows about shifting is still his, and he stays a fixture at the edge of their lives rather than a chapter that closes. Suze ends the book married, still working at the school where she grew up, and clear that becoming an adult with a career has not stopped the dead from finding her.

characters.description: Lena's mother, who never took the cure through three procedures, who was held for years in the Crypts after Portland was told she had killed herself, and who escaped. Lena grew up believing she was dead and has spent the time since learning she was not.
characters.name: Annabel Haloway

characters.description: One of the book's two narrators. She went over the fence out of Portland, survived the Wilds, and now moves with a resistance camp that never stays anywhere long. She has Julian beside her and Alex back from the dead and refusing to speak to her, and she is no longer the girl who wanted to be cured or the girl who wanted to be saved.
characters.name: Lena Haloway

characters.description: Alive, and not the boy Lena knew. He was taken at the Portland fence and held, and what he came out of it with he does not discuss. He is with the resistance, he is civil to everyone else, and he will not look at Lena if he can help it.
characters.name: Alex Sheathes

characters.description: The disowned son of Deliria-Free America's founder, who refused the cure and left the cured cities for Lena and the resistance. He is still learning how to live outside, and he is steady, decent and entirely committed to her.
characters.name: Julian Fineman

characters.description: The woman who found Lena at the border and kept her alive, and who leads their group by hard rules and harder decisions. She has spent years surviving in the Wilds and has no interest in anyone's feelings about it.
characters.name: Raven

characters.description: Raven's partner, quiet, capable and impossible to read, who does the work and rarely explains himself.
characters.name: Tack

characters.description: The book's second narrator, Lena's oldest friend, now cured and living the life the procedure was supposed to guarantee: engaged to the new mayor of Portland, settled, correct and admired. The calm she was promised has not entirely arrived. She dreams, she is restless, and something she did before her procedure will not leave her alone.
characters.name: Hana Tate

characters.description: Hana's fiance, the son of Portland's former mayor and now mayor himself. Young, cured, publicly devout about order and security, and privately used to getting exactly what he arranges for.
characters.name: Fred Hargrove

characters.description: A girl who has joined the camp: capable, cheerful and good in the Wilds. Alex spends his time with her, which Lena notices constantly and says nothing about.
characters.name: Coral

characters.description: One of the homesteaders who came south with Raven's group and stayed. Easy company, and one of the few people Lena can talk to about anything that matters.
characters.name: Hunter

characters.description: Lena's small cousin, the child who does not speak and who found a way to help Lena escape on the night before her procedure. She is still in Portland, in a household that never wanted her and now has one more reason to resent her.
characters.name: Grace

recaps.ending: The resistance attacks Portland and gets inside, and the fighting reaches the streets Lena and Hana grew up on. Raven is killed in it, which takes from Tack and from Lena the person who had held them together since the Wilds. Hana, who has spent the book discovering what her cure did not remove and what her marriage would make her complicit in, breaks with the life arranged for her and helps Lena when it counts, and Grace is got out. By the end the wall around Portland is being pulled down, the cured city is open, and nobody on either side knows what comes next: the government has not simply been replaced, and the country beyond the fences is not organised enough to replace it. Lena and Alex find their way back to each other, and Julian survives what he chose. The book closes without settling the war, on Lena's conviction that the walls people build to keep out what frightens them are the thing that has to come down, and that the tearing down has only started.
recaps.in_short: Told in alternating narration by Lena and Hana. Lena is in the Wilds with Raven and Tack's group, with Julian beside her and Alex, back from the dead, refusing to acknowledge her and spending his time with a girl called Coral. Hana is in Portland, cured, engaged to Fred Hargrove, the city's new mayor, and unable to shake either her dreams or her guilt: before the raid, she gave the regulators Lena's and Alex's names. The government is bombing Invalid settlements and the resistance is bombing the cured cities. Lena's group reaches the crowded stronghold at Waterbury, which is destroyed from the air, and the survivors head north toward Portland for a coordinated uprising. Hana learns what became of Fred's first wife and what her marriage will require of her. The resistance breaches Portland, Raven is killed in the fighting, Hana turns against Fred and helps Lena, Grace is brought out, and the wall around the city is pulled down. Lena and Alex reconcile, and the ending is left deliberately open.

recaps.text: Previously: in a country that treats love as the disease amor deliria nervosa, everyone is cured at eighteen and then assigned a spouse, a job and a number of children. Lena Haloway of Portland wanted the cure until she met Alex, a laboratory guard who was secretly an Invalid living under a forged identity. He showed her the Wilds beyond the border fence, she fell in love, and she learned that her mother had not killed herself but had been imprisoned in the Crypts for years and had escaped. Caught the night before her procedure and freed with her small cousin Grace's help, Lena ran for the fence with Alex; he got her over it and stayed behind, and she believed the guards had killed him. In the Wilds she was found half dead by Raven and taken into a homesteader camp, where a brutal winter killed the child Blue and drove the survivors south. Placed in New York by the resistance under a false name, Lena was assigned to watch Julian Fineman, son of the head of Deliria-Free America. The two were kidnapped, Julian's father left him to die, and Lena went back for him; they escaped together and Julian was disowned by the movement. Then Alex walked in, alive, and looked straight through her.

The book alternates between Lena and Hana. Lena is with Raven and Tack's group in the Wilds, moving constantly because the government has stopped pretending the Invalids do not exist and started hunting them. Julian is with her, still learning how to live outside a city and completely committed to her. Alex is with the group too, alive and unrecognisable in temperament: cold to Lena, careful never to be alone with her, and increasingly in the company of a capable, friendly girl called Coral. Lena says nothing about any of it. In Portland, Hana is cured and about to marry Fred Hargrove, the young new mayor, into the best life the city has to offer. She should feel nothing much about it. Instead she is sleeping badly, dreaming, and finding that the flat calm the procedure promised keeps failing to arrive.

Hana admits to herself what she has been circling: before the raid that ended everything, she was the one who gave Lena's and Alex's names to the regulators. She did it out of fear and jealousy in the weeks before her own procedure, and the cure has not made the fact of it any easier to hold. She begins looking into what happened to the people she informed on. Out in the Wilds, the campaign against the Invalids escalates: settlements are burned and bombed, camps break up and re-form, and the resistance answers with attacks inside the cured cities, which gives the government exactly the justification it wants. Lena's group joins the general movement toward a larger gathering of resistance camps, travelling in worsening conditions with the tension between her, Alex and Julian unresolved.

The group reaches Waterbury, a crowded resistance stronghold swollen far past what it can feed or shelter, full of people who have lost homesteads and are waiting for someone to tell them what happens next. The resistance's leadership is divided over how far to escalate, and the bombings in the cured cities have hardened opinion on both sides of the fence. In Portland, Hana's wedding preparations continue, and she learns that Fred was married before her and that his first wife did not simply disappear. What she uncovers about how that marriage ended tells her precisely what kind of man she is about to be joined to, and what a wife of his is permitted to be. She is cured, she is supposed to be indifferent, and she is not.

Waterbury is destroyed from the air. The stronghold is bombed with thousands of people inside it, and the survivors scatter into the countryside with nothing; the losses are heavy and largely people who had already lost everything once. What is left of Lena's group, with Alex, Julian, Raven and Tack, comes together again afterwards and turns north toward Portland, which is both Lena's home city and one of the government's strongest points. The resistance is no longer trying to survive on the margins: the plan taking shape is to go into a cured city and open it. In Portland, Hana is married into the mayor's household and begins moving through the city with the freedom that gives her, using it for her own purposes.

Hana goes back to the street she and Lena grew up on and finds Grace, Lena's small cousin, living badly in a household that blames her for what Lena became. Fred, meanwhile, orders services cut off to the parts of Portland he considers sympathetic to the Invalids, punishing whole neighbourhoods to force them into line, and Hana watches her husband do it. Outside, Lena's group nears the city and links up with the wider resistance, and Lena comes face to face with her mother, Annabel, who survived the Crypts and has been working with the resistance since she got out. The reunion is nothing like the one Lena imagined as a child. The uprising is set: resistance fighters will move on Portland from outside while the city's own discontent is turned loose from within.

The attack on Portland begins. The resistance breaks through the perimeter and the fighting spreads into streets Lena knows by heart, past her school, her old house and the laboratories. The city's regulators and police are overwhelmed in places and brutal in others, and civilians are caught in the middle of it. Raven is killed in the fighting, a loss that guts Tack and takes from Lena the person who taught her how to survive at all. Hana, inside the city and no longer prepared to be the mayor's wife, moves through the chaos on her own account. Both narrators converge on the same few hours, and the outcome of the whole thing turns on whether Portland's people join the assault or wait for it to be put down.

Portland falls open. The wall around the city is torn down, the cured order breaks in the streets, and what replaces it is nothing anyone has planned: the government is not simply defeated, and the resistance is not organised enough to govern. Hana breaks with Fred and with the life arranged for her, meets Lena again, and helps her; Grace is brought out. Lena and Alex, after a book of not speaking, find their way back to one another, and Julian comes through what he chose. Raven is dead and many others with her. The book ends without resolving the war, on Lena's conclusion that the walls people build to keep out whatever frightens them are the thing that has to come down, and that pulling them down has only begun.

characters.description: A mythical void adventurer who protects his Savannah household. He combines overwhelming combat power with portal travel and takes responsibility for the people who have gathered around him.
characters.name: Derek

characters.description: Cydaria's champion, a powerful fighter, and one of Derek's strongest allies.
characters.name: Alana

characters.description: Derek's bonded void companion, a formidable fighter, and an enthusiastic cook who is treated as part of his family.
characters.name: Silvi

characters.description: An elite Crown fighter, Alana's ally, and Lyra's bonded partner.
characters.name: Avery

characters.description: A prince of Cydaria and a powerful lightning fighter allied with Derek and Alana.
characters.name: Edgar

characters.description: Avery's bonded psionic amphitheer. She is an intelligent dragonkin whose tactical judgment complements Avery's direct approach to combat.
characters.name: Lyra

characters.description: The manager of the Void Emporium and Derek's Savannah household. She oversees the business, its staff, and the practical needs of the people based there.
characters.name: Malorie

characters.description: Savannah's leader and security organizer, responsible for guiding the rapidly growing city through political and commercial change.
characters.name: Natalie

characters.description: A gifted craftsperson at the Void Emporium whose inventive approach joins smithing with related disciplines. Roman teaches her without suppressing her independent methods.
characters.name: Brandy

characters.description: A young fighter in Alana's circle who also shows considerable aptitude for management.
characters.name: Stella

characters.description: A weaponsmith allied with Derek and the maker who helped construct secure containment for dragonkin.
characters.name: the Walking Forge

characters.description: The Walking Forge's worm-like dragonkin companion, associated with the construction of the dragonkin kennel.
characters.name: Rocky

characters.description: A returning guard and trainer connected to Derek's household. He is seeking the people responsible for the kidnapping and murder of his family.
characters.name: Jacks

characters.description: An Indarian royal and established political ally who directs his kingdom's information network.
characters.name: the Indarian duke

characters.description: The operator of Derek's contract shop. His expanding business is nearing a major class upgrade, and he hopes to gain the rare ability to create soul contracts.
characters.name: Rudy

characters.description: A former assassin now serving as a butler in Derek's household. He worries that his old guild could target both him and Ogre outside Savannah.
characters.name: Bones

characters.description: Bones's former associate and another potential target of the Assassin's Guild outside Savannah.
characters.name: Ogre

characters.description: Derek's ward, currently away from the Savannah household while studying at the capital academy. Derek has promised Thomas's grandparents that he will protect him.
characters.name: Thomas

characters.description: A Void Emporium guard who has exchanged binding commoner vows with his pregnant wind-using partner. They plan to establish a home in Savannah while remaining close to the shop.
characters.name: Jax

characters.description: A healer who joined Jax's dungeon party alongside Stella and other young adventurers before the war interrupted their plans.
characters.name: Jensen

characters.description: A senior alchemist and Brandy's mentor. Derek brings him rare monster materials in hopes of developing permanent-stat potions and other valuable products.
characters.name: Roman

characters.description: Roman's assistant and apprentice, an eager alchemical researcher who is keen to test potions.
characters.name: Freia

characters.description: A young, classless fighter training in the capital. She favors water-assisted brawling and is deliberately building skills and affinity before committing to a class.
characters.name: Claire

characters.description: An experienced combat trainer who supervises Claire and her companions as they develop their abilities.
characters.name: Walter

characters.description: The dedicated beast tamer at the secured dragonkin kennel. A member of House Barnes, she has not yet formed a bond and is interested in finding a compatible companion.
characters.name: Lindsay

characters.description: The uncle of an exceptionally durable academy student on Thomas's team.
characters.name: Cain

characters.description: The ancient founder and leader of the Adventurers Guild. He can disperse and reconstruct his molecular body, an extraordinary defensive ability that has preserved him for thousands of years at a lasting personal cost.
characters.name: Klaus

characters.description: A young yellow-lightning fighter training with Claire and his brother Lucas. Their coordinated attacks pair his lightning with Claire's water.
characters.name: Zachary

characters.description: Zachary's brother, a young tank who uses metal magic to extend his shield. He sees protecting Zachary as his central place in their developing team.
characters.name: Lucas

characters.description: An ancient Indarian former elder and immensely powerful sand wielder. Rather than wait quietly for death, he arrives in Savannah while preparing for a final open-ended journey.
characters.name: Marrick

characters.description: A contractor Derek plans to bring along when assessing housing prices for members of his household.
characters.name: Jeffrey

characters.description: The feared identity behind Alana's transformation and controlling voice. Mastering the last skill of this form has let her speak without involuntary influence, but it has also completed the conditions that will force her to leave for another system.
characters.name: Dawn Siren

characters.description: An ancient, intelligent void beast drawn by Derek's Void Call. He speaks, uses Void Steps without a system, and seeks enough self-developed mastery to ascend.
characters.name: Asher

recaps.ending: The Echoing Willow dies under the combined assault of Derek, Alana, Silvi, Avery, Edgar, the Walking Forge, and Rocky. The party receives a World Boss reward and harvests the creature before Linderis can organize a larger response. When a local party attacks, Derek incapacitates most of it and Alana kills its leader, openly confirming that she is the Dawn Siren. Alana has recovered her mother's damaged doll and has only days before ascension removes her to an unknown system. Derek reaches level 245 with every core stat above 1,500, three Origin System skill upgrade points, and one advancement requirement still unmet. Silvi remains at his side, while Avery and Edgar move closer to their own advancement. Asher is still voluntarily training inside Derek's inner void, with his survival and future allegiance unknown. The unassigned dragonkin, Thomas's developing dungeon team, the younger trainees, Marrick's travels, and the unanswered responsibility for Jacks's family remain open as Derek's group prepares to leave Linderis.
recaps.in_short: Back in Savannah after the war, Derek strengthens his household, earns Diamond rank, supports Brandy's inventions, and prepares Thomas and other young fighters for independent growth. Alana then takes him through high-level dungeons, where they devise ways to preserve golem cores and push Derek and Silvi beyond every 1,500-point stat threshold. Alana reveals that she has qualified for ascension and will soon be forced into another system. Derek discloses his origin on Earth and discovers that the Origin System still reaches him. His Void Call attracts Asher, an intelligent void beast who chooses to train inside Derek's inner void. Derek and Alana cross the sea to Linderis, recover the doll Alana's mother made for her, and assemble allies to kill the Echoing Willow. After defeating the World Boss and repelling a hostile party, they prepare to leave before Linderis responds. Derek is level 245 and still lacks one advancement condition, while Alana's departure is imminent.

recaps.text: Previously: Derek became a mythical void adventurer and built a household around the Void Emporium in Savannah. Silvi, his bonded companion, remained both a powerful combat partner and a fiercely independent member of that family. Derek formed close ties with Cydaria's champion Alana, Prince Edgar, Avery, Malorie, Natalie, and the kingdom's royal house. War and invasion drew this circle into conflicts involving Cydaria, Indaria, and hostile nobles. Gerald Torith was defeated, but the larger chain behind the destruction of Jacks's family was not fully exposed. Derek also took responsibility for Thomas, supported Brandy's unusual crafting talent, and helped secure several captured dragonkin whose future bonds remained unsettled. The immediate war ended with political settlements left to the royal families. Derek returned to a Savannah that was safe for the moment, but his own advancement, the danger of the void, the placement of the dragonkin, and the future of the people under his protection all remained unresolved.

Derek returns to Savannah and resumes the practical work of supporting his household. Rudy approaches a class upgrade that may permit soul contracts, while Bones worries that the Assassin's Guild could pursue him and Ogre. Jax and his pregnant partner establish a family and decide to find a home in the city. Brandy's new legendary smithing path produces a working pair of explosive flight boots and a powerful combination of combat skills. Derek also supplies Roman and Freia with rare monster materials under a potion-production agreement. At the dragonkin kennel, Stella and the beast tamer Lindsay emerge as possible future partners for unassigned creatures, although Lyra advises patience. The fate of each bond remains undecided. Meanwhile, Malorie reports that the Void Emporium is profitable after its auction. Natalie allows Derek to buy its site, and he purchases the two adjacent lots as well. The household therefore shifts from wartime survival toward permanent expansion, training, craft development, and preparations for longer journeys.

Derek travels to the capital academy to check on Thomas. After gaining royal authorization to enter, he watches Thomas perform as a capable second-year spear fighter in supervised team combat. Derek spars against students and instructors, demonstrates his control of void techniques, and encourages Thomas to cultivate reliable teammates, especially an unusually resilient tank connected to capital guildmaster Cain. The academy's structure and reopened dungeon access give Thomas a path toward real adventuring experience under controlled conditions. Derek then visits the capital Adventurers Guild to resolve his delayed promotion. There he meets Klaus, the ancient founder and leader of the Guild. Klaus can disperse and rebuild his molecular body, making him exceptionally hard to kill despite the lasting cost of repeatedly altering himself. Derek's void attacks affect that body in a way Klaus has never encountered. After seeing Derek's strength, Klaus grants him Diamond Adventurer rank without a conventional test. Their meeting opens a new line of inquiry into Derek's unusual physical nature and creates a direct connection between him and the Guild's founder.

Klaus studies Derek and concludes that his human and void structures are fused rather than merely layered. In return for permission to examine a regenerated sample, Klaus accepts confidentiality and owes Derek open-ended assistance. Derek declines an offer to lead the Adventurers Guild. He then checks on Claire, Zachary, and Lucas, who are developing a coordinated, skill-first combat style under Walter and Jensen. Claire remains below level ten to strengthen her abilities before choosing a class, while the brothers combine lightning and metal defenses around her water techniques. Back in Savannah, public teleportation between allied kingdoms resumes and Edward becomes king of Cydaria. Brandy improves her flight equipment, Roman and Freia begin contracted potion supply, and the Void Emporium prepares to expand. Marrick, an ancient Indarian sand wielder, arrives instead of waiting passively for death. He befriends Brandy, encourages her to protect her creativity from exhaustion, commissions travel comforts, and sets out on a final open-ended adventure. Derek plans to check on him periodically, leaving Marrick's destination and survival uncertain.

Thomas prepares a regular dungeon party, and Derek gives him escape scrolls for emergencies. As the Void Emporium undergoes a major renovation, Alana finally returns and invites Derek on a circuit of level-250 dungeons. Before beginning, they inspect Cordonia and confirm that Indaria's old exploitative servant contracts have been destroyed and that reforms are taking effect. In a golem dungeon, Derek and Alana discover several methods for shutting down cores without destroying them, creating a valuable source of advanced crafting materials. They also arrange their attacks to slow Derek's experience gain while accelerating his underdeveloped skills. After the first clear, Alana explains the change in her voice and behavior. She is the Dawn Siren, and mastering the final skill of that transformation has given her control over its compulsive influence. The same achievement completed her advancement conditions. A system countdown now means she will soon ascend into an unknown system and leave her companions behind. Bound by restrictions on what she may disclose, she asks Derek to look after Stella. Derek agrees and begins considering how void resources might help the rest of their circle advance.

Derek tells Alana the history he had concealed. He came from Earth, survived its lethal Universal System tutorial, and was stranded in the void after rescuing an ambushed team. When he eventually reached Cydaria, the local system suppressed but could not erase the earlier one. This explains his retained strength, rapid growth, and extraordinary fusion with void power. Alana brings controlled Deathsworn into repeated golem runs so Derek can train skills while receiving only a fraction of the normal experience. Their experiments prove that multiple elements can preserve intact cores, and Derek leaves the highest-level materials with Brandy for future use. He reaches level 242 before shifting to an avian dungeon where Silvi gathers rare cooking ingredients and develops her combat abilities. Derek and Silvi then push their final core stat above 1,500. Derek has now crossed all six thresholds before level 250, but his advancement notice shows one additional condition remains. The local system seeks outside help, and the Origin System answers, granting Derek The Impossible and a large permanent stat reward. Its intervention confirms that the older system still has an active connection to him.

After finishing Alana's remaining puzzle dungeons, Derek turns to Void Call and learns that intelligent, systemless void beasts exist. One such being responds without the usual mindless aggression. In the next encounter, the creature identifies himself as Asher, an ancient void user seeking ascension through his own mastery. Derek discovers that his aura produces fear and a degree of compulsion in Asher, suggesting a deeper authority over void beasts than he understood. Rather than kill him, Derek allows Asher to enter the dangerous inner void space connected to Derek's abilities. Asher chooses to remain there and train, leaving his eventual power and loyalty uncertain. Derek also examines a void beast held in his Time Prison after Void Travel and finds that the combination has catastrophically damaged it. He ends its suffering and abandons the idea of using that method for transport or training. Alana then postpones other travel to complete a final task across the sea. She and Derek reach the Indarian coast and begin the long crossing toward the continent where she was born.

During the sea crossing, Alana decides she cannot safely take her captured wyvern into another system. She will annul the contract before ascending rather than risk lethal bond sickness, leaving the creature's future partner unresolved. Derek and Alana reach the far continent and travel covertly through several kingdoms toward Linderis, where humans and half-elves face severe persecution. Alana briefly confirms that a former party member survived and now leads a powerful noble family, but she avoids revealing herself. Using the local name Alana Brighton, she and Derek pass through neighboring cities and cross the hostile border under concealment. Near the Echoing Abyss, they find fortified camps where Linderis trains nobles and soldiers against mental influence. Derek brings an Indarian duke to investigate and uses his accepted status as a full elf to secure a path through the defenses. The duke confirms that Alana is remembered as a feared legend. At the Abyss edge, Alana reveals that she survived its madness as a child. With only days left before her forced departure, she and Derek descend toward the source of the controlling vibrations.

The Echoing Willow, an immense tree monster, creates the madness that defines the Echoing Abyss. Alana leads Derek to the hidden cave where she survived alone at thirteen and recovers a damaged doll made by her mother, her only remaining possession from her. When the Willow enters a vulnerable interval, Derek summons Silvi, Avery, Edgar, the Walking Forge, and Rocky. Their coordinated attack tears open the trunk, burns the canopy, and floods the roots with lava. Derek attacks from inside while the others prevent the tree from recovering. The Echoing Willow falls and is recognized as a rare, non-respawning World Boss. Derek gains a World Boss achievement, additional Origin System skill points, and reaches level 245. Avery learns why Alana's departure is urgent and discovers that he too is nearing the advancement standard, while Edgar applies his reward toward the same long-term goal. A local party attacks over the Willow's destruction. Derek incapacitates most of them, Alana kills their persistent leader, and she openly identifies herself as the Dawn Siren. The survivors retreat. Derek's group resumes harvesting the Willow and prepares to leave Linderis before a larger force arrives.

characters.description: The officer responsible for an interstellar survey vessel sent to a solar system facing imminent destruction. He must balance the rescue mission against the certainty that the local star will soon explode.
characters.name: The Expedition Commander

characters.description: Specialists drawn from several advanced species who travel to Earth in search of survivors. Their civilization has only recently detected humanity, so the speed of human technological development repeatedly overturns their expectations.
characters.name: The Galactic Survey Team

characters.description: A member of the expedition responsible for interpreting the signals still coming from the abandoned planet. The continuing transmission offers the surface party its best clue to what humanity did before the disaster.
characters.name: The Communications Specialist

characters.description: The inhabitants of Earth, discovered by the galactic civilization only when their sun is close to destruction. They are technologically young by galactic standards but have responded to extinction with an effort on an unexpected scale.
characters.name: Humanity

recaps.ending: The galactic ship follows the automated radio signal away from Earth and discovers that humanity did not remain on its doomed planet. The species has built a vast fleet and launched it toward another star, carrying its population and culture into space without help from the older interstellar civilizations. The rescuers make contact and prepare to guide the refugees to safety. They are astonished that humans advanced from their first detectable radio technology to a planetary evacuation in only a few generations, a rate far beyond the pattern familiar to the galactic community. The mission therefore changes from an attempt to collect a few survivors into first contact with a self-rescued species. The visitors look forward to teaching the newcomers, but the closing perspective undercuts their confidence: humanity's energy and speed may make it a powerful and disruptive force once admitted to the wider galaxy.
recaps.in_short: An interstellar survey ship reaches the Solar System shortly before the sun is due to explode. Galactic civilization learned of humanity only recently and assumes that a species so new to radio cannot escape its planet, so a mixed rescue party descends to Earth hoping to save at least a remnant. The cities are empty. With little time before the stellar explosion, the explorers trace an active signal to an underground installation and discover that it is an automatic beacon rather than a gathering place for survivors. The signal points outward. Returning to space and following it, the expedition finds a huge human migration fleet already traveling toward another star. Humanity has independently built enough ships to evacuate Earth and has escaped before its elders arrived. The rescuers establish contact, impressed and unsettled by the extraordinary speed of human progress. Their assumption that they will simply instruct a primitive newcomer is left looking dangerously complacent.

recaps.text: A galactic survey ship arrives in the Solar System with very little time before the sun explodes. The interstellar community detected Earth's technological civilization only recently and believes the inhabitants cannot yet travel between stars. A rescue party made up of several alien species descends, hoping that shelters or surviving groups may preserve part of humanity. Instead it finds deserted cities and a planet that appears to have been comprehensively abandoned. A continuing radio transmission draws the explorers into an underground installation, but the machinery is automatic and no people are waiting there. The signal is a guide pointing into space. The expedition escapes Earth before the stellar catastrophe and follows the transmission, discovering a vast fleet of human ships heading toward a new star. Humanity has designed and launched its own planetary evacuation within the short period since becoming detectable. The galactic crew makes contact and prepares to help, amazed by a pace of invention that older species have not matched. The rescuers expect to educate the newcomers, while the conclusion suggests that such a rapidly advancing species may soon transform the civilization that believes it is welcoming a pupil.

characters.description: A veteran Earth Forerunner who enters the Wild Hunt with his bonded Eidolon, Erg. Faced with a vast artificial arena and four other human competitors, he begins by searching for Asta while assessing the event's competing routes to victory.
characters.name: Silas Renner

characters.description: Silas's bonded Eidolon and established companion. Erg can manifest beside him inside the Wild Hunt arena, giving Silas a trusted partner from the moment the event begins.
characters.name: Erg

characters.description: An established companion of Silas from before the Wild Hunt.
characters.name: Samvek

characters.description: An Earth Forerunner equipped with a powerful mech suit obtained through outside assistance. She proposes a temporary alliance against Morvarg and says her choices were made to protect her family, though Silas distrusts both her equipment and her apparent ability to influence others.
characters.name: Anika

characters.description: One of Earth's five Wild Hunt competitors and an associate of Anika. At this stage, her agreement is still needed before the proposed human truce against Morvarg can take effect.
characters.name: Nuri

characters.description: An exceptionally dangerous hostile Forerunner whose kills produce unusually large gains. The threat he poses to Earth is serious enough that Anika proposes postponing human rivalries until he is dead.
characters.name: Morvarg

characters.description: Emil's daughter and the Earth Forerunner Silas has been seeking. Long-term alterations from her father changed her into Homo pragmaticum and gave her inherited abilities. She is also a genetic alchemist with a trait that can preserve consenting living beings in spatial storage.
characters.name: Asta

characters.description: Asta's father, whose years of biological modifications shaped her before her induction. His work left her with enhanced attributes, inherited abilities, and a changed human evolution.
characters.name: Emil

characters.description: An Earth Forerunner whose mass-producer occupation can duplicate common objects from a pattern and suitable raw materials. He joins Silas and Asta and accepts a provisional truce against Morvarg while reserving judgment about the other human competitors.
characters.name: Jiang

characters.description: Asta's newly tamed rare Brush Raptor Pack Leader. She names the creature after the party survives its pack, adding a powerful animal companion to the group.
characters.name: Mr. Chompems

characters.description: Leader of the Lepun encountered on Veil. She seeks an alliance with Silas against machine invaders who threaten her people and their sacred groves, offering local guidance in return for human aid.
characters.name: Vex

characters.description: An injured and cursed rare elf Forerunner located at long range by Silas's new drone network. Her condition and position make her the next known rival target in the Wild Hunt.
characters.name: Daina

characters.description: The chained being found inside the Flame Den and targeted by the event under the name Flame Jackal. He rejects that label as a slave name and identifies himself as Yeodirrath, turning an apparent monster hunt into an encounter with a captive who can destroy Erg's manifestation and incapacitate Jiang.
characters.name: Yeodirrath

characters.description: The hunter at the center of the Wild Hunt. He is scheduled to enter the arena after 72 hours at epic tier, accompanied by hounds able to follow prey across realities.
characters.name: The Huntsman

characters.description: Legendary head of the Rayden clan and Samvek's father. Silas summons him through the clan symbol when the Huntsman is about to overwhelm the group, bringing a far stronger ally into the confrontation.
characters.name: Samuel Rayden

characters.description: Silas's inducted sister, already known before this book. Mana is changing her, and Silas has worked to prepare her for the dangers surrounding Earth's induction.
characters.name: Cecilia Renner

characters.description: A United States military leader already connected to Silas before this book. He serves as a conditional ally within Earth's developing defense network.
characters.name: Krulak

recaps.ending: Earth wins the Wild Hunt after Asta voluntarily accepts limited subordination to Silas, following the deaths of Nuri and Anika and the destruction of Morvarg. The Huntsman is freed from Veil, and the artificial world is set to disintegrate. Samuel Rayden survives his clash with the Huntsman by using an escape token. Silas fulfills his agreement with Vex by transporting 986,312 Lepun to Earth and granting them asylum and native status. Their arrival produces a widening high-mana region that disables nearby technology. Earth earned the most points in the event but cannot receive normal induction because it is a contested-sector dungeon world with six incursion slots. Fewer than 34 days remain before induction, while monster attacks and evacuations are already widespread. Cecilia Renner, Asta, Jiang, and human forces defend Normandy, where Silas and Erg destroy an invading force. The communication ban then falls, and Silas commits to leading Earth's response to the approaching war. Anika's children and successor remain his responsibility, the Lepun must be integrated, Yeodirrath's permanent fate is unknown, and Silas and Asta leave their personal relationship undefined.
recaps.in_short: Silas Renner enters the Wild Hunt with Erg and joins Asta and Jiang in a tense alliance with Anika and Nuri against Morvarg. Their campaign on Veil draws them into the Lepun struggle with the Conti Collective and into the Flame Den, where they free bound souls, exploit years of time-dilated training, and defeat the Wild Hunt incarnation of the chained devil prince Yeodirrath. Silas accepts a dangerous devil-derived evolution. Nuri breaks the human oath and dies, Mr. Chompems is killed, and Silas and Erg destroy Morvarg after a struggle involving life, order, chaos, and Veil itself. Anika later dies after transferring her successor right to Silas. The group survives the Huntsman's final pursuit with Samuel Rayden's intervention, and Asta's voluntary subordination gives Earth victory. Silas evacuates 986,312 Lepun before Veil disintegrates, only to learn that Earth is a contested-sector dungeon world nearing induction. He and Erg destroy an invasion at Normandy, communication restrictions end, and Silas accepts an open leadership role in the coming war.

recaps.text: Previously: Silas Renner became a veteran Earth Forerunner and formed a voluntary bond with the Eidolon Erg. His inducted sister, Cecilia Renner, was changing under mana, and he worked to prepare her for the dangers surrounding Earth. Krulak became a conditional ally within the planet's emerging defense network. These relationships leave Silas entering the next crisis with personal obligations to his family and a growing place in Earth's defense.

The Wild Hunt places Earth's five Forerunners in a huge constructed arena and offers victory through eliminating or subordinating their rivals, defeating the Huntsman, or consuming a special prey. Silas begins with Erg and quickly encounters Anika, who proposes a temporary human truce against Morvarg. He finds Asta, learns that Emil's alterations made her Homo pragmaticum, and reunites with Jiang, a mass producer. Asta tames a rare raptor later named Mr. Chompems. The Huntsman awakens early and grows stronger when the competitors fail to kill one another. Silas's group then meets Vex and the Lepun of Veil, whose sacred groves are being destroyed by the artificial Conti Collective. Silas accepts a binding alliance that commits the humans and Lepun to mutual protection and opposition to the Conti presence. Lepun scouts guide the group to a Conti outpost, where Silas must choose between testing the constructs and resuming the search for rival Forerunners. Morvarg makes the Hunt's first Forerunner kill, confirming that the most dangerous rival is already active while the human alliance remains incomplete and distrustful.

All five human Forerunners swear not to harm one another or deny needed support until Morvarg dies, but the oath does not resolve their hostility. A spore attack exploits a loophole and compels Jiang and Nuri to attack allies. Silas cures both without killing them, restoring the group. Two elf Forerunners later ambush Silas and Erg and are killed, giving Earth valuable rewards while provoking an argument over who deserves the gains. Anika and Nuri continue unexplained private activity, deepening Silas's suspicions. Silas builds a clockwork drone, Jiang reproduces it, and their linked reconnaissance network greatly expands Silas's ability to map and identify distant targets. The network locates Daina, an injured and cursed elf Forerunner about fifty miles away. Earth has climbed to third place in world points. As the Hunt's first three days end, a system warning announces dire consequences for failure and introduces a new mandatory threat.

Morvarg attacks plant-world Forerunners near the volcanic region, kills one, and consumes the victim's soul. Silas's group wounds him, but he escapes, and the two rescued Forerunners turn on their rescuers and die. A separate quest identifies Morvarg as a Soul-Reaper and requires Silas to kill him before the Wild Hunt ends. Jiang offers to subordinate himself to Silas if they defeat Morvarg and protect Earth. Inside the Flame Den, the party discovers burned Lepun souls forced into fiery bodies. Silas uses spirit singing to break their chains and free them, gaining a title tied to liberating bound souls. He then evolves his support and healing magic. The dungeon's accelerating time allows the group to train for more than two subjective years while little outside time passes. Silas and Jiang become genuine friends, while Silas and Asta acknowledge mutual attraction but defer a relationship. Asta develops her alchemy, and the party emerges from training much stronger with about eighteen hours left to find the Flame Jackal.

The party defeats a vast volcanic hornet nest, and Asta keeps frozen eggs for a possible future swarm. Battles with hell-mana-infected creatures leave Silas with an incomplete evolution and equipment that increases his connection to dangerous outside power. At the center of the dungeon, the supposed Flame Jackal identifies himself as Yeodirrath and rejects the event's name as a mark of enslavement. He is a bound devil prince and prisoner of war rather than a simple beast. Silas removes two of his restraints but refuses to free him completely. Yeodirrath begins the hunt at a much higher level and chases Silas across Veil. Vex and willing Lepun dead help delay him long enough for the group to reunite. In the final battle, Yeodirrath forces Silas into a struggle over his soul and life essence. Asta and Erg destroy the devil's physical incarnation, ending the event, while Silas saves the critically wounded Jiang. The victory does not establish Yeodirrath's permanent destruction. His blood completes Silas's devil evolution and leaves Silas with 24 hours to accept it or cleanse it.

Silas accepts the aberrant devil evolution, gaining new abilities and a probationary connection to another system. Jiang completes a rare evolution and voluntarily subordinates himself to Silas under reasonable Forerunner commitments. Asta reveals a controlled volcanic hornet swarm. The group then finds Nuri mortally cursed by Morvarg. She attacks Silas and breaks the human oath, allowing Jiang to kill her. The surviving factions converge on Daina and the remaining elf, both of whom die after Silas's team ensures shared rewards. Morvarg arrives wielding an oblivion-like force connected to the remnants of his people. He kills Mr. Chompems and overwhelms the combined attacks of Silas, Asta, Jiang, Erg, and Anika. With aid from Veil and the Lepun, Silas drives life mana into Morvarg's void and is drawn into chaotic space. Order and chaos join life in the struggle, while Erg's bond gives Silas the final connection needed to fill the emptiness. Morvarg and his people are eliminated. Silas returns to Veil after 59 days with new affinities and the title System Intermediary, finding Asta and Jiang far away and Anika marked as hostile.

Silas reunites with Asta and Jiang after his long absence, only to expose their refuge to the Huntsman's hounds. He and Asta's hornet swarm destroy all twelve manifestations, though they will reform. Silas then reaches Anika, who has immobilized Asta and Jiang. Before dying, Anika transfers to Silas the right to choose her successor and identifies the intended replacement for Nuri. Asta and Jiang kill her after she releases them, and Silas accepts responsibility for protecting her children. Rather than end the Hunt immediately through Asta's subordination, the group returns to Vex. They learn that Veil is an artificial fusion of several worlds and that its limits prevent the Lepun from advancing. Silas offers the remaining Lepun asylum on Earth in exchange for long-term nonaggression, cooperation in Earth's defense, and a sacred root for study. The agreement is sworn. The allies destroy the final Conti compounds and recover sacred roots, but the Huntsman confronts Silas and imposes a last test: Silas, Asta, and Jiang must survive as his prey for one full day.

Silas, Asta, and Jiang flee through a landscape controlled by the Huntsman, then ambush and briefly destroy his body. He simply recreates his manifestation, disables Silas, and tears apart Erg's manifested form. Silas summons Samuel Rayden, whose intervention lets the group escape even after the Hunt raises the Huntsman to match the legendary clan leader. Samuel survives through an escape token, and the group completes the 24-hour condition. The Huntsman tells Silas that the struggle freed him from Veil, rewards him, and departs. Veil will now disintegrate. With little time left, Asta voluntarily accepts limited subordination to Silas, completing a victory condition and winning the Wild Hunt for Earth. Silas honors his compact with Vex by transporting 986,312 Lepun to Earth, where their mana disables nearby technology. Earth earned the most points but is an ineligible contested-sector dungeon world with six incursion slots and fewer than 34 days before induction. Silas races to Normandy, joins Cecilia Renner, Asta, Jiang, and human defenders, and destroys an invading force with Erg. Communication restrictions then end as open war approaches, and Silas commits to leading Earth's defense.

characters.description: A young wizard working as a hired investigator for a Chicago detective agency, still early in his career and not yet the established professional he will become. Idealistic, sharp-tongued, and unwilling to look away from a child in trouble, he already shows the reckless compassion and raw magical power that will come to define him.
characters.name: Harry Dresden

characters.description: The seasoned private detective who employs Harry at the Ragged Angel investigations agency. Practical and world-weary, he is focused on doing the job and getting paid, and serves as an older, more cautious counterpoint to Harry's impulsive idealism.
characters.name: Nick Christian

characters.description: A young runaway girl whom Harry and Nick are hired to find and return to her wealthy parents. Frightened and defiant, she has fled home for reasons that make Harry question whether bringing her back is truly the right thing to do.
characters.name: Faith Astor

characters.description: A Chicago police officer who becomes involved in the course of the case, one of the few willing to take an open-minded view of the strange events surrounding it. Tough and direct, she represents Harry's early, uneasy relationship with the city's police.
characters.name: Karrin Murphy

characters.description: A troll, a large and dangerous creature of Faerie, that becomes entangled in the search for the runaway girl and poses a direct supernatural threat Harry must confront to save her.
characters.name: The Troll

recaps.in_short: In this early prequel story, a young Harry Dresden, working as an investigator for the Ragged Angel agency under the detective Nick Christian, is hired to find a runaway girl named Faith and return her to her affluent parents. When they locate her, the job goes wrong: the girl falls into the hands of a troll, a genuine and deadly creature of Faerie, and Harry must use his magic to save her at real risk to himself. In the process he comes to suspect that the home Faith fled was itself the true danger, and that the people paying to retrieve her are not the innocents they appear. A police officer, Karrin Murphy, arrives in the aftermath, an early step in Harry's wary relationship with Chicago's law. Harry rescues the child and, troubled by what he has learned, refuses simply to hand her back to be hurt again.

recaps.text: Early in his career, before he is established as Chicago's professional wizard, Harry Dresden works for a small private detective agency. He and his employer are hired to track down a runaway girl from a wealthy family and bring her home, a routine-seeming job that soon begins to take a darker and stranger turn.

characters.description: A sorcerer who left Ireland after the struggle with Darquesse and has spent five years living quietly in the United States. She returns carrying severe guilt, anxiety, and memories she has never properly faced. Although reluctant to resume her old life, she remains a formidable Elemental and Skulduggery's most trusted partner.
characters.name: Valkyrie Cain

characters.description: A living skeleton, detective, and veteran sorcerer who continues to work for the Irish Sanctuary. Five years after his partnership with Valkyrie ended, he draws her into a new investigation and hopes that working together may help her reconnect with the life she abandoned.
characters.name: Skulduggery Pleasant

characters.description: A student at Corrival Academy who has grown up in the shadow of his celebrated older brother. Omen has little confidence in his own magical ability, but he is observant, decent, and sufficiently overlooked to be useful when Skulduggery needs help inside the school.
characters.name: Omen Darkly

characters.description: Omen's older brother, admired at Corrival Academy as the Chosen One destined to confront the King of the Darklands. He is talented, popular, and generally kind to Omen, even though the expectations surrounding him shape the whole Darkly family.
characters.name: Auger Darkly

characters.description: Omen's quick-witted best friend at Corrival Academy. Never is a Teleporter and shifts between male and female presentation, treating Omen with a mixture of loyalty, teasing, and impatience.
characters.name: Never

characters.description: A teacher at Corrival Academy and an experienced Sanctuary operative. Temper is assigned to watch the school and becomes an adult contact for Omen as the investigation reaches into student life.
characters.name: Temper Fray

characters.description: The Supreme Mage of the Irish Sanctuary and ruler of the sorcerer city of Roarhaven. China has transformed herself from a secretive power broker into a public leader, while retaining the composure and political calculation that have long defined her.
characters.name: China Sorrows

characters.description: A masked combatant working with the Anti-Sanctuary. Lethe's enchanted clothing and disciplined fighting style make him extremely difficult to hit, and his personal interest in Skulduggery's investigation suggests motives beyond simple loyalty to the group.
characters.name: Lethe

characters.description: A member of the Anti-Sanctuary whose magic can erode restraint and encourage the impulses a person normally controls. He is more dangerous as a corrupter than as a direct fighter and gives the conspiracy a way to turn capable opponents against their allies.
characters.name: Smoke

characters.description: A gifted healer drawn unwillingly into the Anti-Sanctuary's plans. Melior's connection to Lethe gives the masked operative a powerful personal reason to keep him alive, while his rare abilities make him valuable to the conspiracy.
characters.name: Melior

characters.description: A Neoteric whose power is strongest inside a place he regards as his home, where he can distort space and the physical rules around intruders. Cadaverous works with the Anti-Sanctuary and takes particular satisfaction in trapping people on ground he controls.
characters.name: Cadaverous Gant

characters.description: An energetic Anti-Sanctuary fighter who carries a pair of lethal parasitic creatures beneath her skin. Razzia is unpredictable in conversation and highly dangerous at close range.
characters.name: Razzia

characters.description: A masked man who calls himself a plague doctor and quietly organizes a small group devoted to finding Darquesse. Sebastian believes she must be brought back, though he keeps both his identity and the reason for his conviction hidden.
characters.name: Sebastian Tao
